style.vernacular: Young creek-and-mangrove capital of Bayelsa (state capital only since 1996): simple single-storey gabled houses of painted render and sandcrete under rusty corrugated roofs in older neighbourhoods, late-modernist white government blocks of the 1990s-2000s around Onopa, newer oil-wealth towers, low flood-prone ground with raised plinths and drainage channels, and bright green palms, mangrove edges and waterways beside most roads.
style.ornament: White late-modernist state buildings with plain colonnaded or canopied entrances, Ijaw heroes monuments and cenotaphs, murals of the Ijaw nation, raised plinths and drainage channels around buildings, and boats, jetties and mangrove banks as the backdrop.
